desc: Parse the input to build the graph and identify all connected components using BFS or DFS.
For each connected component, perform a 2-coloring (bipartite check) to count the number of nodes in the left partition ($L$) and right partition ($R$).
Calculate the maximum number of edges possible for each component as $L \times R$, and sum these up to get $TotalMaxEdges$.
Compute the total number of moves available as $TotalMaxEdges - M$.
If the result is odd, Aoki (first player) wins; otherwise, Takahashi (second player) wins.
Implement the solution in Python: read input, build adjacency list, run BFS/DFS to find connected components and bipartite partition sizes, calculate total moves, and print the winner.
